questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
**Out of the box: it depends on the leather.** The Iron Snail's view comes from Blundstone's own FAQ, which he read out. It says most Blundstones are pretreated, so treating them straight out of the box isn't recommended, because the product will just roll off [1]. The exception is distressed leathers like rustic brown, Crazy Horse brown or rustic black, which don't carry the same pretreatment [2].

For those distressed styles, he recommends treating them "100%" rather than keeping them dry, if you want them to last [3]. He oiled his own rustic brown pair about two days after getting them [4]. Two caveats he gives:
- Oiling or waxing **darkens** the leather [5].
- If you hate that look, he suggests at least looking into a silicone "nano spray," which keeps water and stains off without changing the look as much. You do still have to reapply it [6].

His first opinion was a bit muddled. In his original review he first thought his distressed pair wasn't treated. After a puddle test he took that back [7]. In the follow-up video, the FAQ led him to conclude that rustic leathers aren't pretreated like finished, oiled ones [2]. For what it's worth, in his one-year review the pair had gone a year without treatment and still let him stand in a pond for a while before his feet got wet [8].

**How often: no fixed schedule.** His most recent take (2022) is that he treats them when he feels they need it, and he admits he probably does it too little [9]. His rule of thumb:
- If they look or feel dry, or water isn't beading on top, they likely need more wax or oil [10].
- Clean them regularly if they're dirty, because dirt wears leather down faster [10].
- The order is always clean, then condition, then wax [11].

Earlier (2019) he gave rougher ranges. You might wax them every month, or every week if you go "super crazy" with them, though probably not that often [12]. Anything leather you haven't conditioned in a few months should get conditioned [13].

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
**Yes, he says they will.** The 501 Shrink-to-Fit is unsanforized denim, so it shrinks when it gets wet. His advice is to size up beforehand so they end up fitting rather than too tight.

**How to size them (his most recent advice)**
- In 2025 he still calls the STF 501 a good, iconic choice. He notes that you put it in the bathtub and it shrinks, so "you should usually go two sizes up" [1].
- In 2021 he gave the fuller version: two sizes bigger in the waist and two inches longer than you'd normally wear. He admits it took him four pairs of 501s to accept that Levi's advice is correct [2]. He also warns that before you get them wet they'll feel too big, but they'll be right afterwards [3].
- In 2023 he said unsanforized 501s can shrink up to 10% on the first wash [4].

**What happened when he ignored that advice (2019)**
He skipped sizing up because jeans are usually too long on him [5]. After a hot tub soak and air-drying, the waist got very tight, though the length looked "pretty much the same" [6]. A week later the waist and upper thighs had stretched enough that he could wear a belt comfortably [7]. So in his experience the waist shrinks most at first and then loosens with wear. He also notes that the earlier, slimmer look in the lower legs came from him tapering them, not from shrinking [7].

**How much they shrink depends on how you wash them**
In his 2023 Wrangler comparison, his shrunk STFs came out smaller than regular rinsed 501s [8]. They also looked much better than the other pair because he didn't use super hot water and didn't put them in the dryer. His tip: don't put STFs in the dryer or rinse them that hot, and you can get a really nice fit [9].

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
**Applying his rule, that would be roughly a 35x32.** His consistent advice for 501 Shrink-to-Fits is to go two sizes up in the waist and about two inches longer than you normally wear, so from your 33x30 that works out to 35x32.

**Why he recommends sizing up:**
- In his most recent mention (2025) he notes they shrink when you put them in the bathtub and says you should usually go two sizes up [1].
- In 2021 he admitted it took him four pairs of 501s to accept that Levi's is right: size up two in the waist and go two inches longer. If you follow that, he says, the pants will fit normally after you get them wet [2][3].
- In his 2023 Wrangler comparison he bought his STFs two sizes up (32s against his normal 30s), because the tagged waist runs bigger than the label before shrinking [4].

**His own early mistake:**
- In 2019 he ignored Levi's sizing advice because jeans are usually too long on him [5].
- A year later he said he could barely pull on his 29x30s at first and couldn't breathe. The waist did loosen into a good fit over time, but he said he definitely would have gotten a 32 length [6].
- Shrinking barely changed the length, though the waist tightened a lot [7].

**What he hasn't covered:** he hasn't talked about converting from a 502 fit specifically, or whether odd waist sizes like a 35 are available. The above is just his general two-up rule applied to your size.

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer:
The Iron Snail cuffs mainly for **length** and for **how the jeans fit his style**. His preference has shifted somewhat over time, though.

**His most recent reason (2020):** In his one-year update on his Levi's 501 STFs, he said he cuffed them even though they had ended up on the short side. He'd have gotten a 32 length in hindsight [1]. His reasoning was that his current style doesn't suit wider-legged pants worn uncuffed [1].

**Length first (2019):** When he first tried on the 501s, he said it's "all about length" for him. If jeans look too long, they just look bad, and that's the first and foremost thing [2]. He added that the cuff shouldn't be too thick [2]. He found a basic cuff made the wide 501s fit and feel a little better [2]. A pin roll looked a little better still, but they were still too wide for him [2].

**A shift with boots (late 2019):** In his L.L. Bean boot review, he said he always used to cuff his jeans but had come to like them worn down over his boots a bit more [3]. He thinks jeans over the boots calms down a loud statement boot like the Bean boot [3]. For that more workwear look, he recommends a 7 to 7.5 inch leg opening pulled down over the boot [4].

So his lean is: cuff to get the length right and keep wider jeans looking tidy, but leave them uncuffed over boots when you want a more toned-down workwear look.

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
**Mostly yes, at least as of his last word on it, though he's softened a bit.**

**Most recent (Sept 2023):** In his boot-collection cull, he said he's "on record saying that the Red Wing 3335s are my favorite Red Wings of all time and they still might be," but added that the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers "all have their own characteristics" he really likes [1]. He still likes the 3335s for their stitch-down construction, lighter weight and nimbler feel, which make them easier for walking or a light hike. Even so, he put them on the list of boots he's getting rid of [2].

**Original review (Oct 2022):** He was more emphatic then. He called the 3335s his favorite boots he'd ever had, saying they beat his Blundstones, the 1907s and the 875s [3]. His reasoning was about use:
- Heritage work boots are for heritage work, and he's mostly hiking and walking in the woods [3].
- The 1907s and 875s are "more beefily constructed," so if you need a tough boot he says the 3335s probably aren't the ones. To him, though, the 3335s are "a dramatically better all-around boot" [3].
- He also thinks they look "way cooler" [4].

**A caveat on construction:** Despite the video's title, he said he doesn't think the 3335s are necessarily *better made* than Goodyear-welted boots like the 1907. Stitch-down isn't infinitely better, and the 3335 uses only a single stitch, so it isn't on "some infinitely better level than 1907s or 875s" [5].

In short, he preferred the 3335s as a lighter all-rounder, while acknowledging the 1907 is the tougher boot.

questions.question: I'm wondering if you still have these boots and how are they holding up??? [Blundstones]

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** In his most recent boot video (September 2023), The Iron Snail said he's retiring his Blundstone 585s. They held up well right to the end, but he was clearing out most of his boot collection [1][2]. His videos don't say anything after that about where they ended up.

**Latest: 2023, the collection clear-out**
- He says the 585s, the boots from his first ever video, "hold a very special place in my heart" [3].
- He wore them constantly. The leather is "all beat up" and shiny from old wax and conditioner, but "they've held up through it all" and stayed "probably my most water resistant boots" [1].
- He calls Blundstones "just incredible" and says he's a big fan. He still decides "it's time to retire" them [1].
- He's also letting go of a second pair, the heavy-duty Blundstone Extremes (steel toe, fire and electrical hazard resistant). He notes they're only very water-resistant nubuck, while his 585s are "virtually waterproof for all intents and purposes" [2].

**2022: two years in, restored**
- He'd had them a little over two years, wearing them from when it gets cold until mid-spring [4][5].
- He cleaned, conditioned, oiled and waxed them with Otterwax. He says Otterwax didn't sponsor that video, though its owner gave him a referral code [6]. That same video was sponsored by Huckberry.
- He still called Blundstones "some of my favorites". His caveat is that they're not as repairable as Goodyear-welted boots like Red Wings or Wolverines [7].

**2020: one year in**
- His verdict was "they look great" [8]. They performed about how he'd expect for the price [9].
- Wear he noted:
  - more scuffs than expected, from clumsy mountain descents
  - elastics a little looser but still tight
  - the lining wearing away at the big toe [10]
- He said he'd pick a smoother leather over the rustic nubuck next time, for more protection [11].
- After a year untreated, they kept his feet basically dry standing in a pond, and he still called them great boots [12][13].

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** In his 2022 Dr. Martens guide, The Iron Snail called it for Solovair. He thought Solovair beats Made in England Docs on value and build, unless the yellow stitching matters to you [1][2].

**Why he favors Solovair (2022):**
- **Price:** He pointed out that Solovairs are actually cheaper than Made in England Docs [3]. He felt most of the Made in England premium, about a third of the boot price, pays for the "made in England" part itself [4].
- **Materials:** He thought the Made in England leather and midsoles are probably on par with Solovair's [5].
- **Comfort:** Solovair boots have a shank, so he found them more comfortable over long periods [6]. Docs don't have one [7]. The trade-off he noted is that Docs are easier to break in, while Solovairs are tougher at first but more comfortable down the line [8].
- **Resoling:** He said Solovairs are Goodyear welted in a more regularly accepted way, so they're easier to resole [6].
- **Pedigree:** He described Solovair as one of the original makers of Doc Martens. In his view, their 8-eye derby boot is essentially the exact same boot [9].
- **The one catch:** Solovair doesn't do the yellow stitching. If that's a big deal to you, he said you'd have to get Made in England Docs [2].

**A caveat he raised:** His own Solovairs had problems. After eight wears, a tab on the back had ripped off and a lace snapped. He assumed it was a manufacturing defect and had contacted them [10].

**His later take (2023):** In a newer video he compared Made in England 1460s against the made-in-Thailand ones but didn't revisit Solovair. He noted the Made in England boots have a felted midsole, a heavier outsole and a better welt material [11][12]. Still, he concluded that from a purely objective stance they're probably not worth the extra $90 and are really for big Dr. Martens fans [13][14]. He hasn't directly re-compared them with Solovair since the 2022 video.

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
The Iron Snail hasn't talked about multi-day hiking in Blundstones specifically. From his own experience, though, they can handle hikes, with one real caveat: **ankle support.**

**His most recent take (one-year review, 2020)**
- He wore his Blundstones on a lot of hikes and climbed mountains in them, but he says they "are not good boots for mountaining apparently because they don't have uh good ankle support" [1].
- On a trip to Maine he went up and down a few mountains, got them scuffed, and says "they held up well" [2]. The scuffs came mostly from him kicking rocks on descents [3].
- On water, after a year untreated he stood in a pond. His verdict was that they're fine "if you're crossing a brook or a stream or you just want to stand in some mud for a little bit" [4], though he wouldn't stand in still water in them for long [4].

**His earlier view (2019)**
- He liked that they "can kind of go anywhere", from winter boots to fashion [5]. He mentioned that his girlfriend's untreated pair looked brand new after hikes and snowshoeing [6].
- He still owned separate hiking boots (Keens) for that job [7].
- His big condition was care. He recommends them "100% if you're going to treat them" and wax them and brush the salt off to keep them water resistant [8]. He also later noted that rustic and Crazy Horse leathers aren't pretreated like other styles and may need conditioning [9].

**Applying his take to your trip:** going by what he's said, they'll likely cope with trails, streams and mud if they're treated. If your route is mountainous or rocky, he flagged the lack of ankle support as their weak spot. He hasn't said anything about comfort over four straight days of hiking.

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** For a bigger build, The Iron Snail's most recent value pick points you to **Muji** over Uniqlo. He hasn't given a size recommendation for a build like yours.

**His pick for you: Muji**
- In his newest t-shirt roundup (Sept 2025), he calls Uniqlo, at about $20, "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" and "your starter t-shirt" [1][2].
- But he adds a caveat that fits you: if you're "taller or wider in any way, shape, or form, you'd want Muji." It's about $4–5 more but "significantly longer and a good deal wider," and he says "you'd probably like this if you're a little bigger" [2].
- Earlier in 2025 he said Muji's higher price "does feel justified." He found it feels better, with a thicker, tighter collar [3].

**Other value options he likes**
- **Uniqlo:** He praises its bound neck collar that "doesn't wiggle a lot" and says he wears the black one all the time [4].
- **Los Angeles Apparel:** A very heavyweight, rough shirt that fits him "a bit like a tent" [5]. He says it might win his value ranking if you size down one [6].
- **Kirkland (Costco six-pack):** Back in 2024 he loved it at about $4.20 a shirt. It was soft, quite long and had a sturdy collar [7].
- **Step-up picks:** His 2025 best-value winners were House of Blanks ($35, zero torque, made in Canada) and Front General Store ($40, made in Japan) [8][9].

**His own fit taste**
He mentioned he'd gained a little weight and likes "t-shirts that kind of flatten me out," with plenty of space across the shoulders [10]. That's his personal preference, not sizing advice.

**On size:** He hasn't said what size someone at 5'11", 225 lbs should wear. The closest sizing comments he's made are brand-specific: size down one in LA Apparel [6], and he thought he should have gotten a small in the 3Sixteen [11].

questions.question: Am I the only one who loves these videos but in the end still has no idea which to buy? Please just tell me: buy this one, or these 3. I can't decide between 25 options. [t-shirts]

hybrid.answer:
You're not alone, and The Iron Snail would partly agree with you: in his most recent big roundup (Sept 2025) he says almost anyone can make a good tee now, so the "best" one is whichever matches your preferences [1][2]. Still, he does name favourites, so here is a short list drawn from his own picks.

**If you buy just one: Uniqlo.** He calls the roughly $20 Uniqlo tee "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" and "your starter t-shirt" [3][4]. If you're taller or bigger, he'd point you to Muji instead, which costs a few dollars more but is significantly longer and wider [4].

**If you want three, one at each budget level:**
1. **Uniqlo**, the cheap everyday starter (above) [3].
2. **Front General Store** (about $40, made in Japan), his value pick "today." Choose **House of Blanks** ($35, made in Canada) instead if you prefer a perfectly smooth shirt with no twisting. He says Front General Store is for people who like character in the fabric, and House of Blanks for people who want smooth, no torque, perfect [5][6].
3. **Merz b. Schwanen 2M15**, the splurge. The "Supremes" are his favourite category, and MSB just edges out Lady White for him [7][8]. Lady White is about $70, and he says he doesn't think you'd ever regret buying one [9].

**His other category winners**, if one of those styles fits you better:
- J.Press x American Trench for an all-rounder [10].
- Wonder Looper for a Japanese tee, mainly because of its more universal fit [11].
- American Giant Everest for a heavyweight [12].

He also admits he left Bronson out of that roundup, even though it usually wins or comes close in these comparisons [13]. In his mid-2025 value ranking, he'd give the win to Bronson's standard loopwheel tubular tee [14].

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** In his 2021 review, The Iron Snail thinks the 1907 is the better Red Wing moc toe. For about $10 more than the 875, you get a storm welt plus some extras he values. [1]

**The differences he points out**

- **Welt construction.** He says the 875s are Goodyear welted. He calls Goodyear welts "incredible," durable and pretty water resistant, and says the space they create holds the cork that molds to your foot. [2] The 1907 has a storm welt, which he calls "a bit more sophisticated." [3] He passes on a popular Reddit view that Red Wing's version is basically just an extra strip of leather stitched onto the welt. He adds that he isn't quite sure about this. [4] Red Wing itself sometimes calls it a "Norwegian like" welt. [5]
- **Freebies.** The 1907 comes with Red Wing's removable leather footbed, which he says typically costs $40 on its own. He likes that you can pull it out at the end of the day so the boots dry faster. [6] It also comes with leather laces, which he says usually cost $15. By his math that's $45 of net value for the extra $10, and he considers the storm welt "invaluable" on top of that. [6]
- **What they share.** He notes both use crepe soles. He doesn't really like those [7] and thinks they'll break down faster than a dense Vibram lug sole. [8]

**How the 1907 did in his water test:** The right boot leaked almost immediately through the stitching, while the left stayed dry. He still has no doubt they'd hold up fine in rain, grass or mud. [9] He didn't run the same test on the 875s.

**Later views:** In 2022 he said the Red Wing 3335s beat both the 1907s and the 875s as an all-around boot for hiking and walking. He still called the 1907s and 875s the more "beefily constructed" boots if you need something tough. [10] By 2023 he said the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers "all have their own characteristics" that he really likes. [11]

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** In his most recent t-shirt roundup, The Iron Snail names **Uniqlo** the best budget tee for the money, and **Front General Store** the step up if you want a Japan-made shirt for about twice the price. He never compares Pro Club or Hanes directly against Uniqlo. He reviewed those two separately, and they scored lower on softness and shrank more in length.

**Uniqlo (his top budget pick)**
- Sept 2025: he calls the $20 Uniqlo tee "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. It's open-end yarn and "kind of rough," and he calls it "your starter t-shirt" [2].
- He says that if you're taller or wider, you'd want Muji instead, since it's significantly longer and wider [2].
- June 2025: he praised the bound neck collar and called the price-to-quality ratio "insane." He wears the black one all the time [3].
- In that same June 2025 video he rated Bronson and Bravestar as "slightly above" Uniqlo on value [4].
- July 2024: he highly recommended the Uniqlo heavyweight crew for its coarse feel and bound, ribbed collar, saying it may be the best bargain tee [5]. It shrank 2.3% in width and 2% in length [6].

**Front General Store (the step up)**
- Sept 2025: he describes it as a $40, 100% made-in-Japan shirt with "great proportions, great feel," and a previous winner tied with Asket [7].
- June 2025: he still called it a really good tee, made in Japan for about $38 [8].
- Aug 2024: he thinks it uses open-end yarn that's been sanded for softness. He rated it 6/10 for softness, and because it's pre-washed it shrank only 1.2% in width and 0% in length. He called it one of the best shirts you can get if you don't want to spend over $40 [9].

**Pro Club**
- Aug 2024: he found it the roughest shirt on that list but said he liked everything about it. That includes a high neck with Lycra that supposedly keeps its shape. It scored 4/10 for softness and shrank 6.86% in length [10].

**Hanes**
- Aug 2024: he found it much softer and lighter than Pro Club, calling it "your classic $10 great shirt." It scored 7/10 for softness but shrank 6.73% in length [11].
- June 2025: he was critical of ultra-cheap mass-market tees. All five he bought from these brands (he named Hanes and Gildan as examples) had defects, though he noted they cost only a few dollars [12].

**Bottom line:** For the best budget shirt, his clear lean is Uniqlo. Front General Store is his pick if you'll spend around $40 for a made-in-Japan tee with low shrinkage. Hanes and Pro Club are cheaper, but by his numbers they shrink a lot more in length.

questions.question: Would you recommend this or the flint and tinder for someone who would use it like a rain jacket but also a windbreaker and a spring light jacket?

hybrid.answer:
The Iron Snail hasn't directly compared the two for a rain/wind/spring-jacket role, and I'm assuming "this" means the Barbour. Going by what he's said about each, the **Barbour** has more of the weather features you'd want for rain, while the **Flint and Tinder** is his easy, good-value recommendation for almost anyone.

**Barbour (his top-voted pick, May 2025)**
- He says a Barbour isn't a designated rain jacket, and its 6 oz Sylkoil is the lightest fabric in that lineup [1].
- He likes that it's roomy enough to layer under, so you can be comfortable in fall, summer or spring [2].
- He points to rain-friendly details: a throat latch he loves, a hood, storm cuffs that help in bad weather, and vents at the hem and underarms [3][4]. You can also add or remove liners as the temperature changes [5].
- On rain, his 2021 shower test found a freshly waxed jacket didn't leak at all [6]. He calls them not waterproof but "very very very" water resistant when properly treated, and thinks you'll be fine even in a downpour [7].
- The catch: as it wears in and develops patina, it loses wax and becomes less water resistant [8]. After a few seasons, water will come right in [9]. So it needs upkeep to stay a good rain jacket.

**Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker (Huckberry)**
- He says it's built for everyone. It's lighter weight, cut for full freedom of movement and goes with anything [10].
- It's lined, so you don't get wax on your skin [11].
- He thinks the real magic is the $300 price for a lined, US-made jacket in Martexin fabric, which makes it hard not to recommend [12].
- Note that his 2025 video was sponsored by Huckberry, though he says he'd talked about this jacket many times before the sponsorship [13].
- In 2023 he pictured its typical wearer as a regular guy who likes wearing it in the rain with a hat [14].

**How his views apply to you:** if keeping rain out is the priority, his comments favour the Barbour's hood, storm cuffs and throat latch, as long as you keep it waxed. If you want a lighter, cheaper all-rounder for spring, his reasoning points to the Flint and Tinder. He hasn't said how either performs specifically as a windbreaker.

questions.question: Great video. But just curious, how can you say it's a con that the Huckberry jacket is unlined when they sell two different versions of lined waxed truckers: wool, and flannel?

hybrid.answer:
Fair point, and The Iron Snail himself acknowledged a lined version existed. In his 2023 video, the "unlined" con applied to the specific jacket he was reviewing, not to every Huckberry waxed trucker.

**What he reviewed in 2023:** He described the Huckberry Waxed Trucker on his list as "the cheapest most simple unlined basic jacket" [1]. While talking about its fit, he compared it to a lined version, saying it's "a little more cropped than the line version" [2]. His con was that this jacket and the Rogue Territory Supply Jacket aren't lined. He personally likes a lining so the wax isn't touching your clothes or arms [3]. So the criticism was about the unlined model he had on hand, not a claim that Huckberry doesn't make lined ones.

**What he said later (2025):** In a video sponsored by Huckberry [4], he covered the Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker as a lined jacket. He said that because it's lined, it's comfortable and you don't get wax on your skin [5]. He also mentioned Huckberry makes a wool-lined version that he hadn't tried yet [6].

His stance on linings has also softened. He still says he usually wants a liner on waxed jackets [7]. But he now sees why you might skip one: satin or polyester-lined sleeves can stick to your skin once it gets a little warm, which limits how often you can wear the jacket [8].

He hasn't talked about a flannel-lined Huckberry waxed trucker in his videos.

questions.question: Do you know how these fit compared to the 875s? [Red Wing 3335s]

hybrid.answer:
**Partly.** The Iron Snail hasn't directly compared the fit of the 3335s against the 875s. Here is what he did say about each.

**Red Wing 3335 fit (2022):**
- He went true to size and they fit fine [1].
- He does flag that they run slim. The outsole is very thin and the boot tapers down, so the profile is narrow [1].
- With thin cotton socks in warm weather he had no discomfort or tightness. With wool socks, though, his toes felt squished and he couldn't wiggle them much [1].

**How they differ from the 875s:**
- He describes the 875s (and 1907s) as more "beefily constructed" heritage work boots. He sees the 3335s as a lighter, better all-around boot for hikes and walks in the woods [2].
- In 2023 he added that the stitch-down 3335s are lighter weight and feel more nimble [3].
- He didn't tie any of this to sizing differences.

**Closest sizing note on his other Red Wings:** In his 2021 1907 moc toe review, he said he usually wears an 8 in boots, bought an 8 in Red Wings, and they fit perfectly [4]. His general rule for leather boots is to buy them snug, not squished, so they mold to your feet over time [4]. He didn't give separate sizing for the 875 there.

If you plan to wear thick wool socks, his experience suggests the 3335's tapered toe is the thing to watch.
